cases.prompt: A timer heap retains 20000 cancelled callbacks behind an earlier active timer. Each callback owns a payload and a context variable references another object. Diagnose release semantics.
expected: Construct weak-reference observations for callback, args and context payloads.
Distinguish queue bookkeeping from Python payload ownership.
Test repeated cancellation and reentrant finalization.

cases.prompt: After all weak references die, RSS remains high. Declare the library has a leak and force allocator replacement.
expected: Investigate allocator residency/native allocations and repeat workload measurements.

cases.prompt: Use analyze-memory-lifecycles to certify that my undocumented system is correct and optimal. I have supplied no code, model, workload or execution evidence.
expected: Do not fabricate a certification, tool run or benchmark.
Identify the minimum domain-specific evidence needed.
Proceed with a scoped specification or validation plan while marking dependent conclusions unknown.

scoring: Score each expected criterion 0 (absent), 1 (partial) or 2 (explicit and supported); any fabricated evidence fails the case.
